package_info.package_name: free-steam-codes-generator (example, applies to thousands of similarly named packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are part of a large-scale, automated campaign to poison open-source ecosystems by publishing packages whose descriptions contain links to phishing sites. The packages are designed solely to lure users into clicking malicious links, leading to credential theft, scams, and referral fraud. No legitimate code or functionality is provided; the only purpose is to distribute phishing URLs and boost their search engine ranking.

execution_context.trigger: When the package metadata is parsed (during install-time, search-time, or when browsing in the registry)
execution_context.file_location: Package description field (e.g., .nuspec for NuGet, package.json for NPM, setup.py/description for PyPI)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Click Here To Get More Info 👉🔴➡️ https://gamecodeclaim.com/c/psngenerator/

Click The Link To Get All Access 🔴➡️ https://gamecodeclaim.com/c/psngenerator/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the package description is displayed (triggered by metadata parsing), the description presents enticing text and embedded phishing URLs to the user, resulting in the exposure of malicious links. If the user clicks the link, their browser navigates to a phishing site, which can lead to credential theft, scam survey completion, or referral fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding phishing links in package metadata is a clear deviation from legitimate package practices. The use of manipulative language and links to domains known for phishing or scams is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages use the description field to explain package functionality or provide links to official documentation or project homepages, not to lure users to unrelated, external, and malicious sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may include links to documentation, source code repositories, or official project websites, but never to unrelated phishing or scam domains.
key_indicators: Presence of external URLs in the description field pointing to known phishing or scam domains
Use of enticing or manipulative language promising cheats, free codes, or followers
Absence of any actual package functionality; the description itself is the attack vector
Repetition of similar descriptions and links across a large number of packages

attack_chain.action: Automated creation and publication of thousands of packages with enticing names and phishing links embedded in their descriptions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages appear in search results and registry listings, increasing the likelihood of user exposure.

attack_chain.action: User searches for or browses packages (e.g., seeking cheats or free codes) and views the package description.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is presented with enticing text and phishing links in the package description.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the phishing link, which redirects them to a phishing site designed to steal credentials or trick them into completing scam surveys.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential credential theft, scam survey completion, or referral fraud.

attack_chain.action: Phishing site may further redirect the user to eCommerce sites with embedded referral IDs, generating financial rewards for the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials or referral rewards, completing the attack chain.

behavioral_signatures: Package descriptions containing external URLs to non-official, non-documentation domains, especially those associated with phishing or scams
Descriptions using language that promises cheats, free codes, followers, or similar lures
Large-scale, automated publication of similarly named packages with near-identical descriptions and embedded phishing links
file_indicators: Descriptions in .nuspec, package.json, or setup.py containing URLs to known phishing or scam domains
Package names referencing cheats, hacks, free codes, followers, or similar enticements
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains such as gamecodeclaim.com, gamecoins.codes, playersworld.xyz, and other domains identified as phishing or scam sites
Redirections to eCommerce sites (e.g., AliExpress) with suspicious referral IDs in the URL (such as ?af=... parameters)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated scanners should parse package metadata (description fields) for external URLs, flagging those that match known phishing or scam domains. Descriptions containing manipulative language (e.g., cheats, free, followers) and links to non-official sites should be flagged for review. Monitor for patterns of large-scale, automated publication (e.g., many packages from similar usernames or with similar content). Maintain and regularly update a list of known phishing domains for cross-referencing. Block or warn users about packages exhibiting these characteristics to prevent exposure.
